bundles.title: Bishopric Tool
bundles.description: A ward bishopric’s working tool — meeting programs, assignments, interviews and a members roster.

notes.29: Welcome the newly baptized and those who moved in; releases now come before sustainings.
notes.30: Welcome block first in ward business, with the note beside each name.
notes.31: Every bishopric responsibility on the member's card, not three of five: reminders and responsibilities have their own blocks, the presiding officer gets one, and callings appear at any status rather than only once called.
notes.32: Responsibilities can be assigned to any ward calling, not only the bishopric's three. Assigning to a calling is what gives its holder a card of their own.
notes.33: The callings catalogue carries the assignment names itself, so the separate list of positions is gone — a position is a row in Lookup, beside the organization and calling it belongs to.
notes.34: A position is now named by its own organization and calling, so nothing has to be typed for it and a calling you add in Lookup can be linked to an account straight away. UPDATING AN EXISTING DATABASE: the bishopric's three names change — bishop, counselor1 and counselor2 become bishopric_bishop, bishopric_first_counselor and bishopric_second_counselor. They cannot be renamed in Lists, because the old programme view pins them, so migrate through a file: Settings → export; in the file replace those three names wherever they appear, and add three rows to ref_callings with organization bishopric and callings bishop, first_counselor and second_counselor; then Settings → import that file. Your lists, rows and languages all travel in that file, so nothing else moves. Afterwards, in Lookup, link each position to its account again — the links were keyed to the old list and do not follow. SKIPPING IT IS SAFE: nothing is deleted, every card still appears, and the only loss is that those three show their bare name and cannot be linked until you do it.
notes.36: Ward business follows the General Handbook for priesthood quorum callings. Aaronic Priesthood quorum callings are announced in sacrament meeting without a vote, in a block of their own; they are sustained in the quorum meeting. Elders quorum callings leave the program: the stake presidency presents the presidency, and the quorum sustains the secretary and teachers. The deacons, teachers and priests quorums are now named under the Aaronic Priesthood (for example “Aaronic Priesthood – Priests Quorum – First Assistant”). The bishop is the priests quorum president, so the priests have no youth president, and their first and second counselors become the first and second assistants. UPDATING AN EXISTING DATABASE: an update does not change catalogue rows, so in Lookup, under young_men_priests, rename first_counselor to first_assistant and second_counselor to second_assistant, and delete president.
notes.37: Ward business adds naming and blessing, and confirmation for those baptized but not yet confirmed; quorum callings are announced last. Finnish uses “apulainen” for the priests’ assistants. EXISTING DATABASE: in Lookup, add Welcome statuses child_blessing and confirmed.
notes.38: Aaronic Priesthood quorum callings are announced once set apart (they are sustained and set apart in the quorum), not once accepted.
notes.39: Adds a personal calendar feed: the interviews, calling steps, reminders and sacrament meeting assignments that are yours, in your phone or computer calendar. Subscribe under Settings -> My calendar feeds; each person gets a private link, in the language they pick. What counts as yours comes from the member name and calling linked to your account in Lists. There is no new screen. Links are only issued where the deployment has file storage.
notes.40: The meeting agenda is a list of Sundays beside the open meeting: pick a date to edit that Sunday’s programme without scrolling across a wide table. On a phone a date opens its meeting as its own screen, and Back returns to the list.
notes.41: Programs and Music are now a list of Sundays beside the open one, like the meeting agenda: pick a date to see that Sunday’s whole program, or to edit its hymns. On a phone a date opens its Sunday as its own screen, and Back returns to the list. Printing the music still gives the whole schedule as a table; a program still prints on its own.
notes.42: Shorter pickers: Presiding offers only the bishopric, and Responsible (on the meeting, reminders, interviews, responsibilities and callings) only the bishopric and ward roles such as the executive secretary. Values already saved stay as they are, even ones the picker no longer offers. Visiting authorities are still picked from Visitors. Those bishopric and ward rows can no longer be renamed or deleted in the Lookup tab, since the pickers depend on them.
notes.43: Ward business welcomes the newly baptized and those who moved in under separate words, each in a block of its own.

bundles.title: Our Home
bundles.description: A household chore tracker — points, approvals, rewards, a weekly rota and a shopping list.

notes.18: Adds My calendar: your own chores and weekly tasks, and a Subscribe button that puts them in your phone or computer calendar. Each person gets their own private link, in the language they pick; unsubscribing empties it. Links are only issued where the deployment has file storage.
notes.19: No change in how it works: approved and rejected chores are still filed away after 7 days, and bought shopping after 3; the schema now says so as a duration ("7d").

bundles.title: Team Demo
bundles.description: The widest tour of what the app does: rotations, RSVPs, a board, embeds, doc-views, archived rows and mirrored tables.

notes.5: Adds `teams`, a catalogue whose parent column holds another ROW's id (`hierarchy.by: "id"`) instead of a group's value — so the Lookup tab shows it three levels deep (Acme > Engineering > Backend) rather than the two every other lookup has. Nothing existing changes: `cities` still groups by value, side by side with it, which is the point of shipping both.
notes.6: The navigation is now a set of pages instead of a 22-entry drawer (`nav.layout: "browse"`): the home screen shows tiles for six sections, each section opens as a page of its own entries, and a breadcrumb leads back up. Every screen the old menu had is still there, grouped. Each person can switch back to the side menu under Settings -> Navigation.
notes.7: Settings gains an Appearance section — the theme, plus an icon, image and background for every menu entry — and a single Navigation choice (Side menu, Top navigation, List, Tiles). Their labels now come in Spanish and Swedish as well as English, and the old Background images labels are gone.
notes.8: The rest of Settings now speaks Spanish and Swedish too: the theme colour names, the local-database storage notice, and the Examples dialog.
notes.9: Settings no longer has a Refresh data button (changes from others already arrive on their own), so its labels are gone from the language packs.
notes.10: Drops one of two identical app labels ("No data" in tables and in tiles now share one), so there is one less row to translate. Nothing on screen changes.
notes.11: Adds Notes Gallery under Data: the notes as a grid of picture tiles (`layout: "gallery"`), the first image column as the picture and the title, author and date as the caption. Four more notes, each with a picture, so the grid has something to show. A note without a picture still gets a tile.
notes.12: Adds Take Attendance under Crew: each practice as a card listing who answered, where an organizer marks each person Attended or Absent. A member cannot mark themselves, and once they are marked their RSVP for that practice can no longer be changed. RSVPs now also keep to their own fields (practice, response, note), so a member can no longer write anything else on their response.
notes.13: Check-in with a code: on a day with practices, My RSVP shows one Check-in code box for the whole day. Members type the code shown at practice, or scan it: an organizer can show it as a QR code that opens the app with the code filled in. The code counts for every practice the member answered for that day. The organizer types the same code on their own screen and presses Check in, which marks everyone who entered it as Attended in all of the day's practices. The code is never saved, so it cannot be looked up from home.

bundles.title: Fitness Club
bundles.description: A gym's member app — class booking with door check-in, a training log and stats, memberships, personal training and a workout video library.

notes.1: First release: anyone can open the app and see the timetable, gyms, prices and news without an account; signing in makes you a member-to-be at once, and the member pages open when a membership is active (your history stays through a lapse); book group classes (with a valid membership; the door code needs one too), with places left, a full class refused, and booking from home closing 30 minutes before the start (after that, at the gym); check in to classes by scanning the room code, and log gym visits by scanning the door code; My calendar with your classes, workouts, visits, pauses and PT sessions, where the workout log and gym visits (the latest 5, with Show all), the totals (hours, exercises, visits, km), steps and your top 3 exercises follow the week, month or year the calendar shows; subscribe to your booked classes and workouts in your phone's calendar; coins earned by attending classes (1 per class, plus 1 per streak level reached), spent in a reward shop; buying a membership or a single visit, and pausing it (the pause shows on My calendar across its days, and while it lasts classes cannot be booked or checked in to and the door code is refused); requesting a personal trainer; trainers linked to accounts see their classes and PT clients on their own My calendar; news and a library of workouts and multi-week programmes. Approving a sign-up request makes the person a member in one press. The front desk gets the door code screen, class check-in (the changing code, walk-ins, and ticking people off by hand), membership, PT and reward boards, and statistics (visits, members, attendance by class and by trainer, visits by gym) filtered by gym, class and trainer.
notes.2: Statistics are one view about class attendance only: total attendance, check-ins (booked), walk-ins (no booking), members attending and no-shows, narrowed by gym, room, class and trainer (several of each at once). Gym visits stay on each member's own pages. Rooms now belong to a gym (a Rooms catalogue), so a class offers only its own gym's rooms and two gyms can each have a Main hall. The sample rows now follow today: they are moved so the day they were written for is the day you install them, with four weeks of past classes and ten more members booking them. My calendar is a member's and a trainer's page, so the front desk no longer has it, and adding a workout on a day stays on My calendar instead of opening the workouts table. A class is filed away two hours after it starts: it leaves the desk's lists but stays in members' My calendar, their history and Statistics. The front desk's Class schedule is a page with the same gym, room, class and trainer filters, upcoming and past classes, and Copy events: copy a range of classes (last week, say) to a new start date, as many times over as needed, skipping any already there. Memberships at the front desk is a list instead of a board, with a search for the member and filters by status and plan, so it stays usable with hundreds of members. Booking and class check-in list today and the next two days, with Show more for the days after. A member's own level, coins and pauses count only their own rows, so the front desk's Home no longer shows the whole gym's classes as its level. The menu goes by role, so the front desk can be its own account without being an admin: it sees the Front desk screens and none of a member's own pages, and has no access to members' training. Front desk screens show only to accounts granted their tables, so a door tablet signed in with just the visit log sees the door code and nothing of the desk's.
